summary: CRT-style character output to a buffered FILE stream (fputc/_flsbuf pattern): writes one byte a1 through the stream object a2, switching read-mode streams to write mode, allocating a stream buffer when none is assigned, flushing the existing buffer when full, and falling back to a direct one-byte write for unbuffered streams. Returns a1 on success and -1 with error bit 0x20 set on failure.

operations.description: Validate stream flags at a2[3]: if the write-capable bits 0x82 are clear or the EOF bit 0x40 is set, jump to the error path.
If the read-mode flag (bit 0) of a2[3] is clear, skip the read-to-write mode transition.
In read mode without the own-buffer flag 0x10, take the error path (a switch from read to write requires an assigned buffer).
Clear the read-mode bit with mask 0xFE and reset the stream cursor: *v2 = a2[2] (buffer base into the current-pointer slot).
Rebuild flags: a2[3] = (a2[3] & 0xED) | 2, clearing bit 0x10 and bit 2 and setting bit 1 while marking the stream write-mode.
Allocate the stream buffer only when bits 0x10C of the flags are clear and the stream is not one of the sentinels unk_5E6768 / unk_5E6788 as reported by sub_596007(v4).
Branch on buffered flag 0x108 in a2[3]: buffered write path vs direct one-byte write path.
Buffer-space accounting: v7 = *v2 - (buffer base a2[2]); advance the current-pointer slot by one and set a2[1] = a2[6] - 1.
Buffer full (v7 <= 0): select the per-handle descriptor — unk_5E7898 when v4 is -1, else dword_8D4920[v4 >> 5] + 36 * (v4 & 0x1F).
When the descriptor's text-mode EOF bit 0x20 (byte 4) is set, reposition the handle with sub_58C724(v4, 0, 2).
Flush the previously buffered bytes by writing v7 bytes from the buffer via sub_58E22B(v4, buffer, v7).
Store the output character: *(BYTE*)a2[2] = a1 into the stream buffer slot.
Unbuffered path: write the single byte a1 directly via sub_58E22B(v4, &a1, 1).
On success return a1; otherwise set error bit 0x20 in a2[3] and return -1.
